In this project, I present a novella, which is constructed as a piece of autoethnographic fiction rooted in my experience working in a waiver home in rural Indiana. A waiver home is a kind of residential setting with twenty-four-hour staffing, in which one to five people live who have intellectual disabilities, and, in some cases, physical disabilities as well. The purpose of this project is twofold. The first purpose is to produce a piece of fiction that portrays honestly the experience of people who work in waiver homes in rural Indiana. The second purpose is to provide a close reading of parts of the fiction using preexisting theory, in order to demonstrate the role power plays in the dynamics of waiver home life. The structure of this project is as follows. I discuss how I came to write this piece of fiction, first in a “General Background” section, then in more detail in the literature review, where I also introduce the texts I utilize in the analysis. Following the literature review, I discuss my personal positioning in relation to the issues and topics I discuss and explore in this project. Then, I present the piece of fiction. Following the piece of fiction, I analyze the role of bio-power, risk, and emotion in the fiction. Following the analysis, I present a reflection on notable issues not explored by this project

A waiver home is a residential setting with twenty-four-hour staffing, where one to five people live with intellectual and, in some cases, physical disabilities. The primary purpose of this project is to produce a piece of fiction that accurately portrays the experience of people who work in waiver homes in rural Indiana. ### Budget 2025: A Call for Reform [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]]

The November 26th Budget 2025 is anticipated to come with a significant downgrade to the fiscal outlook, with pressures from recent policy reversals, rising debt-interest costs, and a gloomier economic outlook. It is plausible that annual borrowing could be £20-£40 billion, or more, above the Office for Budget Responsibility's March forecast. This is undoubtedly a challenging outlook for the Government, but it is one that it must respond to robustly. This report considers how tax policy can be used to address the expected shortfall. It sets out a range of options that could together raise over £30 billion, while minimising the economic impact of higher taxes on the economy and living standards. It recommends a strategic approach to reforming the UK's often-distortionary £1 trillion tax system: supporting fair competition between firms; removing biases against workers; and aligning taxes with social and environmental goals. This Budget could simultaneously provide fiscal reassurance, a meaningful Child Poverty Strategy, and long-lasting beneficial tax reform. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]]

sections.heading: emotional ownership and the fan fiction community
paragraphs: Fan fiction writing, or the creation of stories based on popular entertainment franchises, has garnered significant attention from both academic and industry perspectives. While many studies focus on the confrontational aspects of fan fiction writers, it is surprising to discover that these writers often engage in a more nuanced approach to their work. This approach extends beyond mere hostility towards directors and producers; it involves a complex interaction with the broader fan community and the outside world. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] Fan fiction writers have established a vibrant online community, providing a platform for sharing their creations.

This community not only validates their work but also fosters a sense of belonging and emotional connection. The internet has transformed the way these writers interact with each other and the world at large. It has provided a space where they can openly discuss their work, share ideas, and engage in discussions that go beyond the confines of traditional media. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] The impact of the internet on fan fiction writers is profound.

It has enabled them to connect with others who share their passion for the franchise, creating a sense of community and shared experience. This community is more than just a forum for posting stories; it is a place where writers can find support, validation, and a sense of belonging. The internet has also provided a platform for writers to critique each other's work, offering constructive feedback and encouraging a spirit of collaboration and improvement. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] However, the internet has also presented challenges for fan fiction writers.

The sheer volume of fan fiction available online can be overwhelming, leading to a sense of competition and pressure to constantly produce new content. This can sometimes lead to writers feeling like they are not making a significant contribution to the community, which can be discouraging. Despite these challenges, the internet has provided a space where writers can express their creativity and passion, and where they can find a sense of validation and belonging. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] In conclusion, the internet has had a transformative impact on fan fiction writers.

It has provided a space for them to connect with others, share their work, and find a sense of validation and belonging. While it has also presented challenges, the internet has enabled writers to express their creativity and passion in a way that was previously impossible. The nuanced approach of fan fiction writers to their work, combined with the transformative impact of the internet, highlights the importance of understanding the broader context in which fan fiction is created and consumed.

sections.heading: The implications of household size and children for life-cycle saving
paragraphs: IFS: Budget will be 'work of fiction' without Section 7 [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has outlined a budget scenario that hinges on the implementation of Section 7, which is expected to be a key component of the Chancellor's fiscal consolidation plan. Without Section 7, the budget will be described as a "work of fiction," indicating that the measures outlined in the section are crucial for the success of the fiscal strategy. [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The implications of household size and children for life-cycle saving are explored in a study by Econstor. The research, based on fifteen Belgian household budget surveys from 1995/96 to 2010, examines the impact of demographic factors on saving behavior.

The study finds that saving behavior is fundamentally driven by changes in household size and composition, with older individuals being more impatient and thus saving less. This evidence is not clear-cut, but the study presents a more individually based analysis of the data, which challenges the usual practice of assuming a single individual decision maker. [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The Green Budget 2025: Full Report, published by OpenAlex, provides insights into the economic outlook for the UK. Rising productivity and lower interest rates are expected to enable businesses to invest over the medium term, raising the level of investment as firms rebalance their capital-to-labour ratios in favour of capital.

Acting in the opposite direction, fiscal policy is expected to be a headwind to demand throughout the forecast period, as we move from a cyclically adjusted primary deficit of 1.5% in 2025 to a surplus by 2030. This continued fiscal consolidation means that the negative output gap does not fully close by the end of the forecast horizon. [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The Chancellor is expected to be able to deliver the required fiscal consolidation at the upcoming Budget with relatively limited damage to real GDP growth, amounting to -0.25% at peak, and mild disinflation. However, this is predicated on her doing so without applying measures that mechanically or otherwise add substantially to near-term inflation.

The scenario in which the Chancellor delivers a fiscal consolidation through an increase in VAT, raising inflation at a point when inflation is already high enough and central bank credibility is under scrutiny, results in a more significant negative effect on GDP and higher interest rates, requiring a more aggressive easing cycle in 2027.

sections.heading: The macroeconomics of austerity
paragraphs: IFS: Budget Will Be 'Work of Fiction' Without Section 8 [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has warned that the government's budget will be "work of fiction" without the inclusion of Section 8. This section, which is part of the Housing Benefit system, provides financial support for those in need of temporary accommodation. Without it, the IFS predicts that the budget will be significantly reduced, leading to a decrease in public spending and a rise in the national debt. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The IFS's research, published in the UWE Research Repository, uses official figures to demonstrate that the total economic damage inflicted by austerity measures is significantly higher than previously thought.

The study shows that governments since 2010 could have maintained historic rates of growth in public spending and still have reduced Britain's government debt burden by 2019. The austerity measures were not an inevitability, as the global financial crisis of 2008 led to a collapse in capital flows and a halt in world trade. Economic output across rich economies slumped dramatically, causing a significant reduction in public expenditure. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The study's findings suggest that the impact of austerity measures on public spending and the national debt is far greater than previously estimated.

The IFS's research highlights the need for a more comprehensive approach to fiscal policy, which should include the provision of financial support for those in need of temporary accommodation, such as Section 8. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The IFS's warning comes as the government continues to implement austerity measures, which have been criticized for their negative impact on public spending and the national debt. The government has pledged to reduce the national debt by 2019, but the IFS's research suggests that this goal may be unattainable without the inclusion of Section 8. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The IFS's research has been welcomed by those who support the provision of financial support for those in need of temporary accommodation.

However, some critics argue that the government should focus on reducing public expenditure rather than relying on financial support for those in need of temporary accommodation. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The IFS's research has highlighted the need for a more comprehensive approach to fiscal policy, which should include the provision of financial support for those in need of temporary accommodation, such as Section 8.

paragraphs: ### The Budget's Unfulfilled Promise [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has warned that the UK's upcoming budget will be a "work of fiction" without a clear plan to address the £35 billion spending pressures. This warning comes as the government grapples with the economic challenges posed by the ongoing pandemic and rising inflation. The IFS, a respected think tank, has called for a detailed and transparent budget that outlines the government's priorities and how it will manage the financial strain. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The IFS's concern is not just about the financial implications but also about the public's perception of the government's commitment to fiscal responsibility.

The budget, if it is to be considered a work of fiction, will likely fail to meet the expectations of the public, who are already feeling the strain of rising living costs and reduced government support. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The IFS's call for a clear plan is particularly relevant given the current political climate. The government has faced criticism for its handling of the pandemic and the economic recovery, leading to a sense of disillusionment among the public. The IFS's warning suggests that a lack of clarity in the budget could exacerbate this sense of disappointment and undermine public trust in the government's ability to manage the economy.

[[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The IFS's call for a clear plan is not just a matter of transparency but also of accountability. It suggests that the government needs to be more upfront about its priorities and how it will manage the financial strain. This could involve more detailed projections and a clearer explanation of how the budget will be funded and spent. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The IFS's warning is not just about the financial implications but also about the broader implications for the economy and the public's perception of the government's commitment to fiscal responsibility.

The IFS's call for a clear plan is a call for the government to be more transparent and accountable, which could have wider implications for the political landscape. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The IFS's warning is a reminder that the government needs to be more upfront about its priorities and how it will manage the financial strain. This could involve more detailed projections and a clearer explanation of how the budget will be funded and spent.

sections.heading: Green Budget 2025: Full report: evidence angle 10
paragraphs: The Green Budget 2025, a comprehensive report detailing the fiscal and economic strategies for the upcoming year, is set to be a work of fiction without the implementation of Section 10. Rising productivity and lower interest rates are expected to enable businesses to invest over the medium term, raising the level of investment as firms rebalance their capital-to-labour ratios in favour of capital. However, acting in the opposite direction, we anticipate fiscal policy to be a headwind to demand throughout the forecast, as we move from a cyclically adjusted primary deficit of 1.5% in 2025 to a surplus by 2030. This continued fiscal consolidation means that the negative output gap does not fully close by the end of the forecast horizon.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] We expect the Chancellor to be able to make the required consolidation at the upcoming Budget with relatively limited damage to real GDP growth (-0.25% at peak) and mild disinflation. However, this is predicated on her doing so without applying measures that mechanically or otherwise add substantially to near-term inflation. We model a scenario in which the Chancellor delivers a fiscal consolidation through an increase in VAT, raising inflation at a point when inflation is already high enough and central bank credibility under scrutiny, that monetary policymakers are not comfortable looking through the temporary price-level shock for fear of second-round inflationary effects. In this scenario, the negative effect on GDP would be twice as big at its peak as if the same consolidation was done through non-inflationary taxation, and interest rates would remain higher for longer, requiring a more aggressive easing cycle in 2027.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] Households consumption is soft in the near term due to elevated saving. We expect private consumption growth to average 0.9% year on year in 2025, continuing the recent trend for underperformance relative to growth in headline GDP. Consumer confidence remains muted, and household consumption growth is likely to be moderated by a continuation of high saving rates. In Q2 2025, the household saving rate rose to 10.8%.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] It has now risen 7 percentage points from its level in 2022 (4.0%), with the increase focused predominantly in the rate of cash saving, rather than in households' pensions.

faq.question: What does the evidence show about Exploring direct support work through autoethnographic fiction?
faq.answer: ### Exploring Direct Support Work Through Autoethnographic Fiction [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] In this project, I present a novella, constructed as a piece of autoethnographic fiction rooted in my experience working in a waiver home in rural Indiana. A waiver home is a residential setting with twenty-four-hour staffing, where one to five people live with intellectual and, in some cases, physical disabilities. The primary purpose of this project is to produce a piece of fiction that accurately portrays the experience of people who work in waiver homes in rural Indiana. Additionally, the project aims to provide a close reading of parts of the fiction using preexisting theory, to demonstrate the role power plays in the dynamics of waiver home life. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The structure of this project is as follows: I discuss how I came to write this piece of fiction, first in a "General Background" section, then in more detail in the literature review, where I introduce the texts I utilize in the analysis. Following the literature review, I discuss my personal positioning in relation to the issues and topics I discuss and explore in this project. Then, I present the piece of fiction. Following the piece of fiction, I analyze the role of bio-power, risk, and emotion in the fiction. Finally, I present a reflection on notable issues not explored by this project. [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] ### Budget 2025: A Call for Reform [[S3|Mspace (University of Manitoba)]] The November 26th Budget 2025 is anticipated to come with a significant downgrade to the fiscal outlook, with pressures from recent policy reversals, rising debt-interest costs, and a gloomier economic outlook. It is plausible that annual borrowing could be £20-£40 billion, or more, above the Office for Budget Responsibility's March forecast. This is undoubtedly a challenging outlook for the Government, but it is one that it must respond to robustly. This report considers how tax policy can be used to address the expected shortfall. It sets out a range of options that could together raise over £30 billion, while minimising the economic impact of higher taxes on the economy and living standards. It recommends a strategic approach to reforming the UK's often-distortionary £1 trillion tax system: supporting fair competition between firms; removing biases against workers; and aligning taxes with social and environmental goals.

faq.question: What does the evidence show about emotional ownership and the fan fiction community?
faq.answer: Fan fiction writing, or the creation of stories based on popular entertainment franchises, has garnered significant attention from both academic and industry perspectives. While many studies focus on the confrontational aspects of fan fiction writers, it is surprising to discover that these writers often engage in a more nuanced approach to their work. This approach extends beyond mere hostility towards directors and producers; it involves a complex interaction with the broader fan community and the outside world. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] Fan fiction writers have established a vibrant online community, providing a platform for sharing their creations. This community not only validates their work but also fosters a sense of belonging and emotional connection. The internet has transformed the way these writers interact with each other and the world at large. It has provided a space where they can openly discuss their work, share ideas, and engage in discussions that go beyond the confines of traditional media. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] The impact of the internet on fan fiction writers is profound. It has enabled them to connect with others who share their passion for the franchise, creating a sense of community and shared experience. This community is more than just a forum for posting stories; it is a place where writers can find support, validation, and a sense of belonging. The internet has also provided a platform for writers to critique each other's work, offering constructive feedback and encouraging a spirit of collaboration and improvement. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] However, the internet has also presented challenges for fan fiction writers. The sheer volume of fan fiction available online can be overwhelming, leading to a sense of competition and pressure to constantly produce new content. This can sometimes lead to writers feeling like they are not making a significant contribution to the community, which can be discouraging. Despite these challenges, the internet has provided a space where writers can express their creativity and passion, and where they can find a sense of validation and belonging. [[S4|Lund University Publications Student Papers (Lund University]] In conclusion, the internet has had a transformative impact on fan fiction writers. It has provided a space for them to connect with others, share their work, and find a sense of validation and belonging. While it has also presented challenges, the internet has enabled writers to express their creativity and passion in a way that was previously impossible.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The implications of household size and children for life-cycle saving are explored in a study by Econstor. The research, based on fifteen Belgian household budget surveys from 1995/96 to 2010, examines the impact of demographic factors on saving behavior. The study finds that saving behavior is fundamentally driven by changes in household size and composition, with older individuals being more impatient and thus saving less. This evidence is not clear-cut, but the study presents a more individually based analysis of the data, which challenges the usual practice of assuming a single individual decision maker. [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The Green Budget 2025: Full Report, published by OpenAlex, provides insights into the economic outlook for the UK. Rising productivity and lower interest rates are expected to enable businesses to invest over the medium term, raising the level of investment as firms rebalance their capital-to-labour ratios in favour of capital. Acting in the opposite direction, fiscal policy is expected to be a headwind to demand throughout the forecast period, as we move from a cyclically adjusted primary deficit of 1.5% in 2025 to a surplus by 2030. This continued fiscal consolidation means that the negative output gap does not fully close by the end of the forecast horizon. [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The Chancellor is expected to be able to deliver the required fiscal consolidation at the upcoming Budget with relatively limited damage to real GDP growth, amounting to -0.25% at peak, and mild disinflation. However, this is predicated on her doing so without applying measures that mechanically or otherwise add substantially to near-term inflation. The scenario in which the Chancellor delivers a fiscal consolidation through an increase in VAT, raising inflation at a point when inflation is already high enough and central bank credibility is under scrutiny, results in a more significant negative effect on GDP and higher interest rates, requiring a more aggressive easing cycle in 2027.
